reading.rtitle: Proposal: Venice and the Biennale, group of twelve
paras: Thank you for the brief. Below is our proposal for a group of twelve traveling in late September. We have blocked ten rooms at the Ca Bernardi, held until 30 June, and the quote is valid for thirty days from today. If you confirm before the end of the month, we can hold the current rate; if the confirmation arrives in July, the rate will change, because the city applies a different tariff once the Biennale calendar is published.

A word on lead time, because it is the part clients underestimate. Private access to the two pavilions your group asked for requires eight weeks, and the curator-led visit requires ten. We can accommodate a change of date up to four weeks before arrival at no cost. Inside four weeks there is a fee, although we would waive it for a medical reason with documentation. The deposit is thirty percent, and single occupancy carries a supplement of ninety euros per night, which is why we have quoted twin rooms as the default.

Two things we would recommend, based on the last three seasons. First, keep a contingency of one free morning: something in Venice always moves, and a group of twelve moves slowly. Second, if you wanted the same program in October instead, we would build it around the smaller galleries rather than the pavilions, and it would cost roughly fifteen percent less. Our on-site coordinator, Marta, is with the group from the first morning, and she is the person your travelers should call, not the office in Milan.

reading.prompt: What is the main purpose of this message?
choices: To apologize for a price increase that has already happened.
To set out a priced plan with its conditions, and to say what changes if the group confirms late or moves the dates.
To cancel the September dates and offer October instead.

listenings.text: Hello, this is Paolo returning your call about the September group. Two things. The first one is good news: the hotel has agreed to hold the ten rooms until the thirtieth, so you have three more weeks than I told you last time. The second thing is less good. The curator who runs the pavilion visits has moved to a Thursday only schedule this season, so if your group arrives on a Friday, we lose that visit completely. If you could move the arrival to a Wednesday, we would fit both the pavilions and the Thursday visit, and honestly it would make the whole week easier. Let me know either way before Friday, because the deposit invoice goes out on Monday and I would rather send you the right one.

Right, a quick briefing before you all go to bed, because tomorrow starts early. Breakfast is from seven, and the boat leaves the dock at ten past eight and will not wait, so please be downstairs at eight. If you are not there, the group goes and you meet us at the pavilion, which is not the end of the world but it costs you the walk. Bring your passport tomorrow and not your card, because the private access list is checked against passports at the door. Marta is our on-site coordinator, she is Italian, she knows everybody in the building, and she is the person to call if anything goes wrong. Not me, and definitely not the office in Milan. And one more thing: the afternoon is free on purpose. Do not fill it. This city punishes people who plan every hour.
